title: Ink Manufacturing in the US
one_liner: A mature US chemical niche is shifting from publication inks toward packaging, labels, digital inkjet, UV/LED, water-based and low-migration formulations.
overview: The industry manufactures printing and inkjet inks, including lithographic, flexographic, gravure, letterpress, screen, UV/LED and digital ink formulations, and sells mainly to commercial printers, packaging converters, publication printers, office-supply channels and industrial users. The 2022 IBISWorld baseline described a declining industry with 2021 revenue of $3.978 billion after a 2020 COVID-era fall in office and publication printing. Current 2025-2026 market estimates show a firmer nominal picture: the US printing inks market was estimated at $4.69 billion in 2025 and $4.84 billion in 2026, with 2026-2031 CAGR of 3.11%, as packaging and digital workflows offset legacy print contraction.

key_stats.market_size: 2026: $4.84 billion US printing inks market; 2025: $4.69 billion.
key_stats.growth: 2026-2031: 3.11% CAGR forecast for the US printing inks market.
key_stats.packaging_share: 2025: packaging accounted for 56.23% of US printing inks demand.
key_stats.digital_growth: 2026-2031: digital printing process forecast at 4.92% CAGR; 2025 digital inks reached 15% of label volume in the cited market estimate.
key_stats.price_index: June 2026: BLS/FRED printing ink commodity PPI was 276.601, up from December 2025 at 267.951.
key_stats.baseline_imports: 2021: IBISWorld baseline imports were $7.311 billion and imports satisfied 69.1% of domestic demand.

baseline_2022.market_size: 2021: $3.978 billion revenue in the January 30, 2022 IBISWorld baseline, in 2021 dollars.
baseline_2022.growth: 2016-2021: -5.0% annualized revenue decline; 2021: -2.5% decline; 2021-2026 baseline forecast: -2.4% annualized decline to 2026 revenue of about $3.5 billion.
baseline_2022.profit: 2021: $96 million profit and 2.4% profit margin in the IBISWorld baseline.
baseline_2022.exports: 2021: $711 million exports; 2026 baseline forecast: $638.5 million exports.
baseline_2022.imports: 2021: $7.311 billion imports; 2026 baseline forecast: $6.2 billion imports.
baseline_2022.product_mix: 2021: nonimpact digital inks were 28.9% of industry revenue; lithographic and offset inks were 6.0%.

how_it_makes_money: Manufacturers formulate and blend pigments, resins, solvents, oils, additives and carriers into inks and related coatings, then sell recurring volumes to packaging converters, label printers, publication and commercial printers, screen printers, distributors and OEM-linked digital-print customers. Revenue depends on production volume, custom color/formulation work, compliance-sensitive applications such as food packaging, and pass-through pricing for pigments, resin, energy and freight.
cost_structure: Purchases are the largest cost category because ink production depends on petroleum-derived solvents, oils, resins, pigments, plastic/resin inputs, additives and packaging. Labor is meaningful but smaller than materials in a capital- and chemistry-driven process; the 2021 IBISWorld baseline showed $580 million in wages. Profit is thin and volatile: the baseline showed a 2021 profit margin of 2.4%, while 2025-2026 supplier announcements point to renewed pressure from pigments, nitrocellulose, energy, tariffs, freight and chemical feedstock availability.
current_dynamics: The demand base is splitting. Publication and office-linked inks remain structurally weak as newspapers, magazines, catalogs and paper-heavy office workflows lose volume. Packaging is now the center of gravity: 2025 packaging represented 56.23% of US printing inks demand, with growth supported by food, beverage, pharma, e-commerce corrugated and labels. Formulation is also changing as customers demand low-migration, recyclable, water-based, UV/LED, electron-beam and bio-based options. Cost pass-through remains active in 2025-2026 because pigment tariffs, nitrocellulose constraints, energy markets and freight lanes continue to affect input costs.
whats_growing: Packaging inks, labels, corrugated flexographic inks, water-based systems, UV/LED curable inks, low-migration food-contact inks, electron-beam and other low-VOC technologies, digital inkjet inks for short-run labels and on-demand books, and specialty inks for textiles, industrial graphics and printed electronics.
whats_shrinking: Publication inks for newspapers and magazines, lithographic and offset inks tied to long-run print media, solvent-heavy gravure where VOC rules and sustainability audits make reformulation necessary, and commodity office-print demand exposed to paperless workflows and hybrid work.
recent_developments: 2026-03-19: Sun Chemical announced immediate price increases and surcharges across all product divisions due to energy, logistics and chemical feedstock pressures.
2026-03-26: Flint Group rebranded as Flint Group Packaging Solutions to emphasize packaging, sustainable inks, coatings and digital print consumables.
2026-01: Canon U.S.A. introduced Texas LT3 Series UV LED flatbed printers, reinforcing downstream demand for UV LED ink systems.
2025-07-23: Flint Group launched Flexocure LEAP UV inks for lower photoinitiator migration risk in food packaging.
2025-07-01: Flint Group expanded resin production for NC-free flexible-packaging inks, citing a 30% production-capacity increase at the Caronno site.
2025-05-05: Sun Chemical announced tariff surcharges on color materials, including pigments imported into and produced in the United States.
outlook: The 2026-2031 outlook is better than the 2022 baseline decline forecast in nominal market terms, but the industry is not returning to a broad print-media growth cycle. The healthiest producers will be those with packaging exposure, compliance know-how, digital inkjet portfolios, domestic or diversified pigment/resin supply and enough scale to absorb testing, regulatory and working-capital burdens. Expect consolidation pressure to persist among smaller commodity ink makers, while larger global suppliers invest around packaging, low-VOC chemistry, UV/LED, bio-based resins, conductive inks and supply-chain localization.
themes: Packaging replaces publishing as the core demand engine
Digital inkjet and short-run labels outgrow legacy lithographic print
Low-VOC, water-based, UV/LED and low-migration chemistry become competitive requirements
Pigment, resin, nitrocellulose, tariff and freight volatility drive price actions
Domestic sourcing and supply-chain resilience gain importance
Industry consolidation continues as scale matters for compliance and R&D

title: Inorganic Chemical Manufacturing in the US
one_liner: A mature, energy-intensive manufacturing industry supplying chlorine, caustic soda, soda ash, acids, catalysts, carbon black and other mineral-based inputs to chemicals, construction materials, paper, glass, rubber, water treatment and refining.
overview: The industry converts mineral, salt, sulfur, phosphate, natural gas and electricity inputs into basic inorganic chemicals used by downstream manufacturers. Demand is broad but not insulated from cycles: chemical producers, PVC and glass makers, paper mills, refiners, tire and rubber manufacturers, water-treatment users and construction-material suppliers all drive volumes. The 2022 IBIS baseline showed a mature, consolidated industry with $34.0 billion of revenue and a 6.2% profit margin. By 2025, external market estimates put the US inorganic chemical manufacturing market at about $40.5 billion, but 2026 operating commentary points to uneven demand: caustic soda remains supported by alumina, pulp and paper and water treatment, while chlorine derivatives, PVC and titanium dioxide remain exposed to global oversupply, imports and weak construction demand.

key_stats.industrial_chemical_output: 2025: chemical materials industrial production index 100.9459, up from 98.7455 in 2024
key_stats.electricity_cost: 2025: US industrial electricity price averaged 8.62 cents/kWh
key_stats.natural_gas_cost: 2025: Henry Hub averaged $3.52/MMBtu; 2026 EIA forecast near $3.67/MMBtu
key_stats.import_price_pressure: June 2026: other basic inorganic chemical import price index 65.4, Dec. 2022=100

how_it_makes_money: Operators sell bulk and intermediate inorganic chemicals by tonnage, purity, contract reliability and logistics capability. Revenue comes from long-term supply contracts and spot sales of chlor-alkali products, caustic soda, chlorine, soda ash, inorganic acids, potassium and sodium compounds, chemical catalysts, carbon black and related products. Large integrated producers also capture value by consuming chlorine internally in vinyls, chlorinated organics or other downstream chains while selling caustic soda, hydrochloric acid, bleach, hydrogen and co-products externally.
cost_structure: The cost base is dominated by raw materials, electricity, natural gas, plant maintenance, depreciation, environmental compliance, transport and labor. Chlor-alkali production is especially power intensive because salt and electricity are core inputs; the 2025 US industrial electricity average of 8.62 cents/kWh and the 2026 Henry Hub forecast near $3.67/MMBtu keep energy procurement and hedging central to margins. The 2022 baseline showed profit at 6.2% of revenue and wages at $4.1 billion, while competitive commodity pricing limits the ability to pass through cost spikes quickly.
current_dynamics: The industry entered 2026 with mixed demand. ACC’s June 2026 outlook expects overall US chemical output to rise only 0.5% in 2026, with basic chemicals up but inorganic chemicals declining. Caustic soda is the relative bright spot because alumina, water treatment and pulp and paper demand remain active. Chlorine-linked chains are weaker because PVC, vinyls and some construction-related derivatives remain under pricing pressure. Import prices for other basic inorganic chemicals remain far below late-2022 levels, indicating continued global price pressure even as US energy and electricity costs remain material.
whats_growing: 2025-2026: caustic soda demand tied to alumina, pulp and paper, water treatment and chemical processing
2026: US basic chemical output expected to rise 1.2%, although inorganic chemicals are expected to underperform within the group
2025-2031: US inorganic chemical manufacturing market forecast CAGR of 4.1%
2026-2027: US LNG exports and manufacturing reshoring investment support medium-term demand for advantaged US chemical chains
whats_shrinking: 2026: inorganic chemical output is expected to decline within basic chemicals, according to ACC’s mid-year outlook
2025-2026: PVC, vinyls and chlorine derivatives remain pressured by weak construction and global oversupply
June 2026: import price index for other basic inorganic chemicals at 65.4 versus Dec. 2022=100 signals sustained pricing compression
2025-2026: titanium dioxide remains pressured by excess Chinese capacity and weak China demand
recent_developments: 2025-12-15: Westlake announced December 2025 closures including a Lake Charles diaphragm chlor-alkali unit with 825 million lb/year chlorine and 910 million lb/year caustic soda capacity.
2026-01-26: Tronox announced plans to close a 46,000 metric ton/year TiO2 plant in China due to weak demand, sulfur costs and excess Chinese TiO2 output.
2026-01-30: Olin said global caustic soda demand remained healthy, led by alumina, water treatment and pulp and paper, while its 2026 chlor-alkali outlook remained challenging.
2026-06-12: ACC forecast US chemical output up 0.5% in 2026, with basic chemicals growing but inorganic chemicals declining.
2026-07-17: BLS/FRED showed the other basic inorganic chemical import price index at 65.4 for June 2026, down from the Dec. 2022 base of 100.
outlook: The 2026-2027 outlook is low-growth and margin-sensitive rather than broadly expansionary. Revenue should be helped by caustic soda, water treatment, reshoring-linked manufacturing investment and eventual recovery in durable-goods and construction demand, but chlorine derivatives, TiO2 and other globally traded products face oversupply and import-price pressure. Producers with low-cost power, integrated chlor-alkali/vinyls assets, logistics scale and disciplined capacity management are best positioned. Smaller or less integrated plants remain exposed to energy costs, environmental compliance and commodity price swings.

title: Insect Repellent Manufacturing
one_liner: A small, seasonal US chemical-products niche making sprays, liquids, wipes, lotions and treated products that repel mosquitoes, ticks and other biting insects.
overview: The industry manufactures skin-applied and surface or gear-applied insect repellents for consumer use, including liquid sprays, aerosols, wipes, gels, creams, lotions and specialty formats. The baseline 2022 industry was small and highly concentrated, with $332.0 million in revenue, 15 enterprises, 18 establishments and 250 employees. Domestic production is constrained by offshoring and import competition, while branded demand remains resilient because repellents are a low-ticket seasonal purchase linked to public health guidance. For 2025, the narrow US manufacturing market is estimated at about $337.0 million using the baseline 2022-2027 forecast path, while broader US consumer insect repellent market estimates are materially larger because they include imported finished goods and retail value, with published 2025 estimates ranging from $403.4 million to about $1.97 billion depending on scope.

key_stats.market_size: 2025 estimated US insect repellent manufacturing revenue: $337.0 million, derived from the 2022 baseline of $332.0 million and the 2022-2027 forecast CAGR of 0.5%.
key_stats.growth: 2022-2027 forecast CAGR: 0.5% for US manufacturing revenue; broader US consumer insect repellent market growth estimates include 5.3% CAGR for 2026-2033 in one 2025 dataset.
key_stats.profit_margin: 2022 baseline EBIT margin: 7.8%; 2027 baseline forecast EBIT margin: 7.4%.
key_stats.imports: 2022 baseline imports: $283.4 million, equal to 54.8% of domestic demand; 2027 baseline forecast imports: $400.8 million, equal to 64.1% of domestic demand.
key_stats.exports: 2022 baseline exports: $98.4 million, equal to 29.6% of revenue; 2027 baseline forecast exports: $116.2 million, equal to 34.1% of revenue.
key_stats.broader_market_reference: 2025 broader US insect repellent market estimates: $403.4 million in one consumer-goods dataset and about $1.1 billion to $1.97 billion in other broader retail/category datasets, reflecting different category definitions.

baseline_2022.profit: $26.0 million profit in 2022, equal to a 7.8% EBIT margin.
baseline_2022.product_mix: 2022 revenue mix: liquid repellents 52.1%, gels/creams/other repellents 31.1%, aerosol repellents 16.8%.

how_it_makes_money: Manufacturers earn revenue by formulating and packaging active ingredients such as DEET, picaridin, IR3535, PMD/OLE, citronella and newer botanical actives into branded and private-label products sold through drugstores, mass merchants, home centers, grocery stores, outdoor retailers, e-commerce channels and wholesalers. Revenue is concentrated in spring and summer sell-in, with warmer Southern states, Hawaii, travel use and outdoor recreation creating steadier demand. Larger firms also monetize brand portfolios, retailer shelf space, export channels, institutional/public-health applications and adjacent pest-control products.
cost_structure: The largest operating costs are chemical and botanical inputs, solvents, propellants, packaging, aerosol cans, bottles, wipes, caps and labels, followed by contract manufacturing or plant operating costs, logistics, retailer allowances, marketing, quality assurance, regulatory testing and EPA registration compliance. The 2022 baseline shows a small labor base, with wages of $21.1 million against $332.0 million of revenue. Profit was 7.8% of revenue in 2022 and was forecast at 7.4% in 2027, supported by brand pricing and higher-margin natural products but pressured by import competition, tariff exposure, petrochemical inputs and seasonal inventory risk.
major_players: Spectrum Brands Holdings Inc. / Cutter and Repel
Avon Products / Skin So Soft Bug Guard
Chase Products Co. and other private-label or contract manufacturers
current_dynamics: Demand is being pulled in two directions in 2025-2026: public-health messaging around mosquito and tick bites supports category relevance, while weather, tariff uncertainty and retailer inventory timing can make sell-in volatile. EPA-registered products remain the trust anchor because CDC guidance directs consumers to EPA-registered repellents and EPA lists major approved skin-applied active ingredients. Branded leaders are defending shelf space with DEET, picaridin, OLE/PMD and family/outdoor formats, while smaller brands push botanical, aluminum-packaged, fragrance-light and premium formulas. Manufacturing economics remain weaker than retail category demand because imports and multinational supply chains capture much of US consumption.
whats_growing: Picaridin products, oil of lemon eucalyptus/PMD products, premium DEET-free sprays, family and sensitive-skin formats, travel-size products, wipes, outdoor recreation channels, e-commerce, private label, public-health-driven use cases and export demand are growing. EPA-listed 2026 active-ingredient counts show continued depth in DEET products, with more than 500 registered products, plus about 40 picaridin products, about 45 IR3535 products and 1 listed 2-undecanone product.
whats_shrinking: The number of domestic manufacturers, domestic employment, lower-differentiation commodity production and some chemical-heavy or odor-heavy legacy formulations are under pressure. The baseline forecast called for enterprises to fall from 15 in 2022 to 12 in 2027 and employment to fall from 250 in 2022 to 232 in 2027. Domestic production share is also shrinking as import penetration was forecast to rise from 54.8% of domestic demand in 2022 to 64.1% in 2027.
recent_developments: 2025-01-30: CDC updated mosquito and tick bite prevention guidance, again directing consumers to use EPA-registered insect repellents and noting US tick exposure is most active from April to September.
2025-02-04: SC Johnson announced high-speed manufacturing lines in Nairobi for Guardian spatial repellent, with stated capacity of up to 20 million units annually.
2025-05-21: SC Johnson highlighted Mosquito Shield and Guardian spatial repellents, citing clinical-trial evidence that Mosquito Shield used with bed nets reduced malaria disease risk by 33%.

2025-08-07: Spectrum Brands said fiscal Q3 2025 Home & Garden sales were hurt by tariff-related supply constraints, stopped shipments to some retailers and wet, cool early-summer weather that delayed replenishment orders.

2025-11-13: Spectrum Brands reported fiscal 2025 net sales down 5.2% and said Home & Garden returned to topline growth in Q4 after a delayed season, while fiscal 2026 guidance expected flat to low-single-digit net sales growth.
2026-01-23: EPA updated its skin-applied repellent ingredients page, listing DEET, picaridin, IR3535, PMD/OLE, citronella, catnip oil and 2-undecanone among EPA-registered active ingredients.
outlook: Through 2027, the baseline points to only modest manufacturing growth, with revenue forecast at $340.4 million and a 0.5% 2022-2027 CAGR. The better growth story is at the consumer category level, where disease awareness, warmer mosquito seasons, tick range expansion, outdoor recreation and premium natural formats support higher retail sales. Domestic manufacturers still face a structural ceiling from offshore production, import penetration, retailer bargaining power and the need to fund testing and compliance for EPA-regulated claims. Winners are likely to be brands and contract manufacturers that can combine efficacy, regulatory credibility, supply-chain reliability and clean-feel or botanical positioning without sacrificing protection time.

one_sentence: US insect repellent manufacturers sell EPA-regulated consumer protection products into mass retail, pharmacy, outdoor, grocery and private-label channels, with demand tied to mosquito and tick seasons, vector-borne disease awareness, outdoor recreation and the shift toward picaridin, OLE/PMD and other lower-odor or botanical formulations.

title: Institutional Pharmacies
one_liner: Closed-door pharmacies serving hospitals, nursing homes, assisted living, hospice and other care facilities are growing with senior-care demand but remain squeezed by drug costs, reimbursement rules and consolidation.
overview: Institutional pharmacies sit behind hospitals, skilled nursing facilities, assisted living communities, behavioral health facilities, hospice and other institutional care settings, supplying medications plus compliance packaging, medication-regimen review, clinical consulting, formulary support, delivery, billing and regulatory assistance. The industry is mature and reimbursement-sensitive, but its demand base is defensive because residents in nursing and senior-care settings usually require recurring medication management. The 2022 IBIS baseline reported $20.98 billion of revenue and 4.7% 2022 growth; a 2026 Guardian Pharmacy filing cited IBISWorld’s 2025 U.S. institutional pharmacy revenue estimate of about $24.3 billion, implying roughly 5.0% annualized growth from 2022 to 2025. Current conditions are shaped by recovering facility occupancy, high drug inflation in specialty and chronic-care categories, Medicare Part D redesign in 2025, and continued M&A among national and regional long-term-care pharmacy providers.

key_stats.market_size: $24.3 billion in U.S. institutional pharmacy revenue in 2025
key_stats.growth: About 5.0% CAGR from 2022 to 2025, inferred from $20.98 billion in 2022 baseline revenue and $24.3 billion in 2025 IBISWorld estimate cited in Guardian Pharmacy’s 2026 filing
key_stats.long_term_care_drug_spend: $22.276 billion of U.S. long-term-care prescription drug expenditures in 2025, up 7.8% from 2024
key_stats.nonfederal_hospital_drug_spend: $42.932 billion of U.S. nonfederal hospital prescription drug expenditures in 2025, up 9.6% from 2024
key_stats.certified_nursing_facility_occupancy: 79% U.S. certified nursing facility occupancy in July 2025, up from 77% in July 2024 and 72% in July 2022
key_stats.senior_housing_occupancy: 89.9% senior housing occupancy in 2Q 2026 in NIC MAP data
key_stats.total_health_spending: $5.3 trillion U.S. national health expenditure in 2024, up 7.2% from 2023; CMS projects 5.4% average annual NHE growth for 2025-2034

baseline_2022.growth: 4.7% revenue growth in 2022 and 1.42% CAGR from 2004 to 2022
baseline_2022.product_mix: 2022 revenue mix: 57.9% brand-name prescription medications, 13.8% generic prescription medications, 5.1% nonprescription medications, 23.2% other services

how_it_makes_money: Revenue comes mainly from dispensing prescription drugs to institutional residents and patients, then receiving reimbursement from Medicare Part D plans, Medicaid, commercial insurers, facilities and private-pay residents. Operators also earn service revenue from compliance packaging, medication carts and unit-dose systems, 24/7 clinical support, medication-regimen reviews, therapeutic interchange, formulary management, infusion support, vaccination clinics, regulatory consulting, billing support and analytics tools that help facilities manage medication spend and reduce adverse drug events.
cost_structure: The largest cost is pharmaceutical purchasing from manufacturers and wholesalers; Guardian reported cost of goods sold equal to 79.8% of revenue in 2025, down from 80.1% in 2024. Labor is the next major cost because pharmacies need pharmacists, technicians, delivery staff, account managers, billing specialists and clinical consultants. SG&A, technology platforms, regulatory compliance, delivery fleet costs, insurance, rent, equipment, software, interest and acquisition integration costs also matter. Margins remain thin because payors pressure reimbursement rates, generic substitution can lower revenue per claim, and operators must meet CMS long-term-care pharmacy service requirements.
major_players: PharMerica / BrightSpring Health Services: BrightSpring reported $11.446 billion of 2025 Pharmacy Solutions revenue and 43.367 million prescriptions dispensed in 2025.
Omnicare: CVS’s long-term-care pharmacy subsidiary entered Chapter 11 in September 2025, and a court approved sale of the business to GenieRx Holdings LLC in May 2026.
Guardian Pharmacy Services: reported $1.449 billion of 2025 revenue, 61 pharmacies, about 205,000 residents served and about 8,400 LTC facilities across 38 states at year-end 2025.
Regional and independent LTC pharmacies: Guardian’s 2026 filing said the market includes several regional providers and more than 1,200 independent pharmacies.
Specialized providers such as Remedi SeniorCare and regional closed-door pharmacy operators compete in selected skilled nursing, assisted living, behavioral health and hospice markets.
current_dynamics: The demand backdrop improved through 2025 and 2026 as certified nursing facility occupancy rose to 79% in July 2025 and senior housing occupancy reached 89.9% in 2Q 2026. Drug cost inflation and mix shift toward specialty, GLP-1, oncology, behavioral health and chronic-care therapies are raising revenue per prescription but also intensifying working-capital and reimbursement risk. Medicare Part D redesign in 2025 capped beneficiary out-of-pocket spending at $2,000, eliminated the coverage gap and shifted more liability to plans and manufacturers, changing plan economics and pharmacy network negotiations. Consolidation remains active: Guardian acquired pharmacies in 2025, BrightSpring’s pharmacy segment grew 31% in 2025, and Omnicare’s 2025 Chapter 11 and 2026 court-approved sale show the stress on large LTC pharmacy models.
whats_growing: Assisted living, behavioral health, memory care and home- and community-linked pharmacy services are growing as senior housing occupancy climbed to 89.9% in 2Q 2026 and Guardian increased residents served from 186,000 in December 2024 to 205,000 in December 2025. Compliance packaging, medication-adherence analytics, psychotropic-drug monitoring, antibiotic stewardship, medication-spend analysis and disease-state management are growing as facilities look for measurable clinical and cost outcomes. Specialty and higher-priced chronic drugs are lifting revenue per script: BrightSpring’s pharmacy revenue per script rose 26% in 2025 to $263.93.
whats_shrinking: Available senior-care capacity is tightening: NIC reported only 0.4% annual inventory growth in senior housing in 2Q 2026, and its October 2025 release said fewer than 1,400 new units opened in 3Q 2025. Standalone skilled-nursing-focused models face pressure from litigation, reimbursement and drug-cost volatility, highlighted by Omnicare’s September 2025 Chapter 11 filing. Traditional low-touch dispensing without analytics, clinical intervention, cost containment or compliance support is losing relevance as facilities and payors demand documented value.
recent_developments: 2025-01-01: Medicare Part D redesign took effect with a $2,000 annual out-of-pocket cap, elimination of the coverage gap and a new manufacturer discount program.
2025-05-14: Guardian Pharmacy acquired Senior Care Pharmacy in Wichita, Kansas, expanding its Midwest LTC pharmacy footprint.
2025-06-02: Guardian Pharmacy acquired Washington-based Mercury Pharmacy Services, adding a Pacific Northwest LTC pharmacy presence.
2025-09-22: Omnicare, a CVS Health subsidiary, initiated voluntary Chapter 11 proceedings to address litigation and broader LTC pharmacy financial challenges.
2026-03-11: Guardian Pharmacy reported 2025 revenue of $1.449 billion, up 17.9%, with residents served rising to about 205,000.
2026-05-13: A bankruptcy court approved the sale of Omnicare’s business to GenieRx Holdings LLC, a joint partnership of Milrose Capital and Integro Healthcare Services.
outlook: The 2026 outlook is modestly positive but uneven. Revenue should keep expanding because U.S. health spending is projected by CMS to grow 5.4% annually over 2025-2034, Medicare spending is projected to grow 7.7% annually over 2025-2034, senior housing occupancy reached 89.9% in 2Q 2026, and long-term-care prescription drug expenditures grew 7.8% in 2025. Profitability will depend less on volume alone and more on purchasing scale, payor contracting, automation, delivery density, clinical programs and the ability to manage expensive drug mix under Part D and Medicaid rules. Expect further consolidation, more tech-enabled clinical services, and continued pressure on operators unable to secure favorable reimbursement and drug acquisition terms.
one_sentence: Institutional pharmacies dispense, package, deliver and clinically manage medications for residents and patients in facilities without their own pharmacies, with 2025 revenue estimated at $24.3 billion and demand supported by higher long-term-care occupancy, Medicare Part D coverage and rising prescription-drug spending.

title: Insulation Contractors
one_liner: Insulation contractors install thermal, acoustic and mechanical insulation in buildings, making the industry a rate-sensitive specialty trade tied to housing starts, commercial construction and energy-efficiency retrofits.
overview: Operators install, replace and maintain fiberglass, mineral wool, polyisocyanurate, polystyrene, cellulose, spray foam and other insulation in residential, commercial, multifamily, municipal and industrial buildings. The baseline IBISWorld file defines the industry as establishments primarily engaged in installing insulation products for buildings, excluding insulation work performed by general building contractors. Demand is mostly project-driven: new construction creates the largest work packages, while remodeling, weatherization, energy-code compliance, HVAC/mechanical insulation and rebate-funded home upgrades support retrofit work. The industry remains highly fragmented, price-competitive and local, with low capital intensity but meaningful labor, safety and material-handling requirements.

key_stats.market_size: 2024 revenue was estimated at $9.8 billion; baseline 2022 revenue was $13.466 billion in 2022 dollars.
key_stats.growth: 2024 revenue was expected to grow 1.4%, while 2019-2024 revenue fell at a 1.4% CAGR; baseline 2022 revenue growth was 1.4%.
key_stats.profit_margin: 2022 baseline profit margin was 6.7%; a later public report page estimated 2023 profit at 7.3% of revenue.
key_stats.employment: 2022 baseline employment was 83,237 workers; BLS reported 67,400 insulation-worker jobs in 2024 across floor/ceiling/wall and mechanical insulation occupations, with 2024-2034 employment growth projected at 4%.
key_stats.establishments: 2022 baseline establishments were 27,955 and enterprises were 27,768.
key_stats.housing_starts: 2025 total housing starts were 1.36 million, down 0.6% from 1.37 million in 2024; May 2026 starts ran at a 1.177 million seasonally adjusted annual rate, down 8.7% from May 2025.
key_stats.construction_spending: May 2026 private residential construction spending was $930.2 billion SAAR and private nonresidential construction spending was $738.7 billion SAAR.
key_stats.labor_pay: BLS reported 2024 median annual wages of $48,680 for floor, ceiling and wall insulation workers and $57,250 for mechanical insulation workers.

baseline_2022.growth: 2022 revenue was projected to rise 1.4%, with 2017-2022 revenue growing at a 2.5% CAGR.
baseline_2022.profit: 2022 profit was $902 million, equal to a 6.7% margin.
baseline_2022.product_mix: 2022 revenue mix was fiberglass 50.4%, polyisocyanurate 17.6%, polystyrene 17.5%, mineral wool 11.3% and other alternative materials 3.2%.
baseline_2022.major_markets: 2022 residential building work generated about 49.0% of revenue and commercial building construction generated about 26.5%.

how_it_makes_money: Contractors earn revenue by bidding labor-and-material installation packages for home builders, remodelers, commercial builders, multifamily developers, HVAC/mechanical contractors, property owners, municipal clients and energy-retrofit programs. Jobs are priced through fixed bids, unit pricing, time-and-materials work or subcontractor packages, with revenue driven by installed square footage, material type, access complexity, code requirements, schedule pressure and whether the work is new construction, retrofit, mechanical insulation, fire-stopping or acoustic insulation.
cost_structure: The cost base is labor-heavy and project-variable. In 2022, baseline wages were $4.036 billion, about 30.0% of $13.466 billion revenue, and profit was $902 million, or 6.7% of revenue. Material purchases include fiberglass batts and blown-in fibers, spray foam chemicals, mineral wool, rigid foam boards, vapor barriers, fasteners, protective coverings and disposal supplies; contractors also incur insurance, workers compensation, vehicles, tools, scaffolding, safety equipment, fuel, estimating, warranty, subcontractor and compliance costs. BLS 2024 wage data show labor pressure from median pay of $48,680 for floor/ceiling/wall insulation workers and $57,250 for mechanical insulation workers.
major_players: Regional independent insulation contractors and nonemployer subcontractors
current_dynamics: The 2025-2026 operating environment is mixed. Residential new-construction demand weakened as 2025 housing starts slipped to 1.36 million and May 2026 starts fell 8.7% year over year, pressuring contractors tied to single-family builders. Retrofit work is better supported by the 2023-2025 Energy Efficient Home Improvement Credit, DOE Home Energy Rebates and aging housing stock. Nonresidential work is uneven but supported by manufacturing, data-center, healthcare, education and energy-code-driven building-envelope upgrades. High financing costs, tight skilled labor, insurance costs and competitive bidding continue to limit margins, while stricter energy codes and demand for acoustic, fire-resistant and HVAC/mechanical insulation create higher-specification work.
whats_growing: Retrofit insulation, air sealing, attic upgrades, weatherization, multifamily efficiency projects, HVAC duct and pipe insulation, acoustic insulation, mineral wool, polyiso, EPS and code-compliance work are growing. The US HVAC insulation market was estimated at $2.03 billion in 2025 with a projected 2025-2030 CAGR of 4.6%, and the US building thermal insulation market generated $7.0675 billion in 2025 with a projected 2026-2033 CAGR of 5.0%.
whats_shrinking: Single-family new-construction insulation packages are under pressure because 2025 single-family starts fell 6.9% from 2024 and May 2026 total housing starts were 8.7% below May 2025. Lower-spec commodity fiberglass work is also more exposed to price competition, while do-it-yourself air-sealing materials can capture some small retrofit spending when homeowners use the 2023-2025 tax credit without hiring a contractor.
recent_developments: 2024-08: Public market-research release estimated US insulation contractors revenue at $9.8 billion in 2024, up 1.4% for the year but down at a 1.4% CAGR over 2019-2024.
2025-01: IRS updated Energy Efficient Home Improvement Credit FAQs, confirming 2025 insulation and air-sealing eligibility at 30% of costs up to $1,200.
2025-02: NAHB forecast 2025 residential remodeling growth of 5% and 2026 growth of 3%, offsetting weaker multifamily starts.
2026-02: NAHB reported 2025 total housing starts of 1.36 million, down 0.6% from 2024, with single-family starts down 6.9% and multifamily starts up 17.4%.
2026-04: Walls & Ceilings published its 2026 Top 25 Insulation Contractors list, highlighting national consolidators and regional specialists.
2026-07: Census reported May 2026 construction spending at a $2.2102 trillion seasonally adjusted annual rate, 1.5% below May 2025.
outlook: The 2026 outlook is cautious but not uniformly negative. New single-family work is likely to remain soft until mortgage rates and builder financing improve, while multifamily, commercial, institutional, manufacturing and retrofit channels should provide offsetting demand. Energy codes, utility programs, DOE rebates and the 2023-2025 federal tax credit pull insulation toward higher-performance building-envelope work, but the expiration or modification of tax incentives after 2025 is a key policy risk. Over the next several years, contractors with scale, estimator discipline, trained crews, rebate-program eligibility and capability in air sealing, mechanical insulation, mineral wool and continuous insulation should outperform commodity residential installers.
themes: Commercial, HVAC and acoustic insulation resilience
one_sentence: The US insulation contractors industry is a fragmented construction specialty trade that was $13.466 billion in 2022 baseline revenue and an estimated $9.8 billion in 2024 public-market-research revenue, with 2025-2026 demand split between weak single-family construction and stronger retrofit, multifamily, HVAC and nonresidential energy-efficiency work.
